_doc: Battle 20 (Andrew Jackson) geodata for the 3D worlds. x, y = BASE frame units (ajackson/data/frame.json: web mercator z10, origin [64288,104976], x east, y south; 132.5 m/unit at New Orleans, 128.3 m at Horseshoe Bend). A region of zoom z uses x * 2^(z-10). Built by ajackson/tools/make_geo.py from OSM lines + the research files; Jackson's line fitted onto the OSM Rodriguez Canal (see the places' notes).

places.name: Villere plantation house (British HQ 23 Dec-19 Jan)
places.src: Estimate: ~9 mi below the city (Latour p.95; Remini 1999), ~3 mi downriver of Rodriguez Canal; NPS hh29h: Villere house British HQ 23 Dec-19 Jan
places.note: Gabriel Villere escaped through a window ~11:30 a.m. 23 Dec (Latour p.87) | remapped onto the real river bank (research placed it on a straight line; the river bends south below Chalmette)

places.src: Latour p.95: anchored 'on the brink of Villere's batture opposite the centre of the British encampment, within musket-shot'; opened 7:30 p.m.
places.note: Sunk by British hot shot 27 Dec (NPS hh29i; Wikipedia) | remapped onto the real river bank (research placed it on a straight line; the river bends south below Chalmette)

places.name: Horseshoe Bend (Tohopeka peninsula), centre
places.src: NR 1975 + NHD river geometry; peninsula points SOUTH, river on E/S/W sides, neck on the north
places.note: Tallapoosa River, Tallapoosa Co., Alabama. Park centre per Wikipedia 32.9727,-85.7359.

places.name: Breastwork (barricade) centre
places.src: NPS National Register nomination, Horseshoe Bend Battlefield (Stout & Kretschmann 1975), UTM 16N converted to WGS84 (item 6, UTM 16/618170/3648970)
places.note: Log breastwork across the neck; 5-8 ft high, double rows of portholes (Jackson to Blount). Length: NR 250 yd, CLR 300-400 yd, EoA/Wikipedia ~400 yd (use ~350 m / 'nearly 400 yards'). Zig-zag/angled, concave to the south (Cheatham map; Waselkov). Park marks it with white posts since ~1969; archaeology 1964/1973 confirmed line.

places.name: Tohopeka village site
places.src: NPS National Register nomination, Horseshoe Bend Battlefield (Stout & Kretschmann 1975), UTM 16N converted to WGS84 (item 4, UTM 16/617620/3648200); CLR 'at the toe of the peninsula'
places.note: ~300 log houses; refugee village of Red Sticks and families; burned by Cherokee/allied Creeks during the battle. Cherokee canoe action interpreted at Tour Stop 3 at the toe.

places.name: Gun Hill (Jackson's artillery position)
places.src: NPS National Register nomination, Horseshoe Bend Battlefield (Stout & Kretschmann 1975), UTM 16N converted to WGS84 (Congressional Monument, UTM 16/618120/3649100; moved ~50 ft west in 1965) + CLR
places.note: Small eminence N of barricade. Jackson to Blount: nearest ~80 yd, farthest ~250 yd from the works (Jackson to Pinckney: 150-200 yd). One 6-pdr + one 3-pdr, opened ~10:30 a.m. for ~2 h. Maj. Lemuel Montgomery's grave (reinterred 1972) is on Gun Hill; he died at the wall.

places.name: Cotton Patch Hill (Jackson's approach overlook)
places.src: CLR 2013 (highest point in park, view south to barricade); position approximate from Visitor Center 32.9823,-85.7354
places.note: Army arrived here the morning of 27 Mar 1814 (NPS 'The Overlook'). Carroll map: first US line ~400 yd N of barricade (2 h), second 300 yd (1.5 h), third at the wall (8 min).

places.name: Park Visitor Center / Highway 49 entrance
places.src: Wikimedia Commons geotag, Category:Horseshoe Bend NMP Visitor Center
places.note: Modern; not for the map. Gives the north (approach) side.

places.name: Bean's island (Lt. Jesse Bean, 40 men)
places.src: NPS National Register nomination, Horseshoe Bend Battlefield (Stout & Kretschmann 1975), UTM 16N converted to WGS84 (Miller Bridge UTM 16/617720/3649200 spans the west arm next to the island); CLR Tour Stop 1
places.note: Island 'due west of the peninsula' in the Tallapoosa; Bean's men sank fleeing Red Sticks before they landed (Coffee to Jackson, 1 Apr 1814).

places.name: Cherokee canoe crossing (south toe of peninsula)
places.src: CLR p.21 (120-yard swim) + NPS Tour Stop 3 'Cherokee Crossing' at the toe; position inferred from NHD tip (32.9661,-85.7407)
places.note: Three Cherokees led by Tuq-qua ('The Whale') swam, took Red Stick dugout canoes, ferried others (Capt. Russell's spies, Col. Gideon Morgan, Maj. John Walker, ~30 others); ~200 Cherokee crossed per NPS. NOT verified: 'Charles Reese' (found in no source here; use 'The Whale / Tuq-qua').

places.name: Coffee's mounted brigade, south bank (approx. line)
places.src: CLR p.20: line 1/4 mile back from the river on the south bank; Holmes/Jackson maps. Position schematic
places.note: 700 mounted + ~600 allies (500 Cherokee, 100 friendly Creek) crossed 2 mi BELOW the bend at an island ford, turned upstream, ringed the loop from W through S to E.

places.name: Coffee's river crossing (2 mi below bend, island ford)
places.src: CLR p.20 ('two miles below the bend at an island ford'); river distance computed on NHD chain from the bend exit
places.note: Exact ford not documented; schematic.

places.name: Hammond's rangers (east bank, opposite Tohopeka/east arm)
places.src: CLR p.20-21 (Capt. Eli Hammond defended the riverbank opposite Tohopeka). Schematic

places.name: Jackson's camp night of 26 Mar (6 miles from the bend)
places.src: CLR p.20 ('within six miles of the bend', square camp of brush and trees); direction N/NW from Fort Williams road. Schematic
places.note: Army left 06:30 on 27 Mar.

places.name: Emuckfaw Creek mouth (on the Tallapoosa)
places.src: USGS NHD (Emuckfaw Creek flowline end)
places.note: Just downstream (NW) of the bend. Battle of Emuckfaw 22 Jan 1814 was fought up the creek (~33.00,-85.73), Jackson's Jan campaign; Enotachopo Creek 24 Jan (Hillabee town) is a different creek further SW.

places.name: Emuckfaw battleground (approx., up the creek)
places.src: NHD creek course + Cheatham map ('previous battleground along Emuckfau Creek'); Wikipedia geotags it at the park (imprecise)
places.note: Approximate.

places.name: Newyaucau (New Youka) village site
places.src: NPS National Register nomination, Horseshoe Bend Battlefield (Stout & Kretschmann 1975), UTM 16N converted to WGS84 (item 5, UTM 16/619970/3649840)
places.note: Upper Creek town, 'burned before the battle'; its people joined the refugees at Tohopeka. Across the river from Coffee's position upstream.

places.note: Supply depot on the Coosa at Cedar Creek, built 22 Mar 1814; site now under Lay Lake (modern reservoir; do not draw). 52-mile trail to the bend.
